what_this_changes: The weighing protects the inputs it was computed from, which are the positions inside their tolerance on the text the step started on, and leaves the update free wherever those inputs carry little; with the damping at the low end of what single precision reads, that freedom is large. The answers written again leave the step's text within their first tokens, so the stepped model stands on inputs the weighing never held. A balance against what one token's update does to the others has to be read on the trace the stepped model has, not on the text before the step (Marcos's point relayed at 7:21 AM CT November 15: the loss is measured on the trace the model has after the update). This closes the weighing as built here, with its damping read on the old text; it does not establish that a weighing with its damping read on answers written again, or more of it, does no better, and it says nothing against regenerating and correcting again, which the plain loop does at the same steps.
